newsitem.title: GREECE: NIKIFOROS BROKERAGE SAYS LICENCE REVOCATION UNFAIR.
newsitem.headline: NIKIFOROS BROKERAGE SAYS LICENCE REVOCATION UNFAIR.

text.p: Athens bourse member Nikiforos Brokerage which had its licence revoked by the capital markets commission last week said the decision was unfair and planned to fight it in court.
"We were deeply surprised (by the decision). There were no substantiated violations of regulations and authorities' promises to us fell through," its president Fokion Skabavias said in a statement.
He said the licence revocation was "unfair and illegal" and will cause irreparable damage to the firm which will seek to return to the bourse.
Greece's capital market commission revoked the licence of Athens stock exchange members Epsilon Securities and Nikiforos Brokerage on May 27.
The commission said that Epsilon was found to have serious financial difficulties, poor organisational structure and internal compliance procedures.
"These weaknesses and breaches render the company's continued operation risky for the investment public and the smooth functioning of the capital market," the commission said.

Similarly, Nikiforos Brokerage lost its licence for all of the above reasons including deficiencies in internal procedures that were found inadequate for the safeguarding of securities held on investors behalf.

"Besides, the firm had violated securities regulations related to the Delta Securities-Tryfon-Georgakis affair. These violations render the company dangerous for the investment public," the statement said.
